ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The licensed Samoan registered agent must screen every proposed director, shareholder, UBO, and account signatory against (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List (Resolution 1267/1989 and 1988 regimes); (ii) the US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List; (iii) domestic Samoa terrorist designations administered by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit under the Counter-Terrorism and Transnational Organised Crime Act 2006; and (iv) consolidated European Union and United Kingdom financial sanctions lists. Screening must occur at engagement, immediately before incorporation, and periodically thereafter on a rolling 90-day basis. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and persons linked to PEPs must be identified through enhanced due diligence, commercial PEP database checks, and open-source verification; any PEP relationship requires senior management approval, documentation of source of wealth and funds, and ongoing transaction monitoring. For this CRO engagement, source-of-funds verification must include the executed clinical trial sponsor agreement, the milestone payment schedule, and bank references; all incoming milestone wires are verified against the declared payee and invoicing structure. Any hit, false positive, or suspicious alert is escalated to the registered agent's AML Compliance Officer and reported to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit as required by law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry — Companies and International Companies Registry Division, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia; name reservations and company registrations are filed by licensed registered agents through the Registrar of International Companies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be registered in Latin script (English or Gagana Samoa). A Chinese or other non-Latin script version may be adopted only as a parallel trading name; it does not replace the registered Latin-script legal name. The chosen name must be distinguishable from all existing and reserved names; names that are phonetically equivalent or visually similar are treated as conflicting.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Samoa (requires prior consent of the Registrar)
Clinical Trial / Drug / Medical (requires prior approval of the Ministry of Health where the name implies regulated medicinal activity)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the licensed registered agent must file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of International Companies within 10 working days of the notice, setting out distinctiveness and compliance arguments; the Registrar must respond within 14 working days. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may file an appeal to the Supreme Court of Samoa by originating motion within 21 days of the reconsideration decision (Judicature Ordinance 1961), or concurrently re-file a modified name containing additional distinguishing tokens within 7 days of rejection at a nominal re-filing fee. Reserved names may not be extended beyond 30 days unless an incorporation filing is pending before the Registrar.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as a stand-alone solution. The International Company must maintain a registered office in Samoa at a physical address (no post-office box) and retain a licensed Samoan registered agent at all times. The registered agent's physical premises may serve as the registered office; the CRO's clinical trial management operations may be conducted entirely offshore without leased Samoan premises. Pure 'virtual office' mail-forwarding services lacking a physical Samoan address do not satisfy the International Companies Act 1987.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated at under 10% probability in the first two years of operation. Primary inspection risk attaches to the licensed registered agent, which is subject to periodic AML/CFT on-site examinations by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and the Central Bank of Samoa on a 2–4 year cycle; unannounced inspections are permitted under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007. The offshore CRO's clinical data and milestone invoicing functions do not create material on-site inspection exposure in Samoa.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss. 5-15 (incorporation), s. 12 (registered office), s. 20 (shares and capital), s. 73 (registered agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1 (Memorandum and Articles of Association of an International Company) with Statement of Compliance and Registered Agent's Consent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued at par or premium, and no escrow or paid-up capital deposit is required under the International Companies Act 1987.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriber to the Memorandum of Association subscribes for all initial shares at par value, and that the share register be duly executed. RESOLVED, that until otherwise determined by the Board, the registered office of the Company shall be established at the address of the registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and that the registered agent is authorized to file all documents required by the International Companies Act 1987. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as Director, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Principal Officer, each to serve until retirement or resignation, and that any two officers are authorized to execute banking and clinical trial contract documentation for the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the SIFA online portal or in person at the SIFA registry counter in Apia. Provide an original certificate of incorporation of the ultimate parent (if any) and a short explanatory note confirming that the proposed name does not imply connection with the Government of Samoa or any regulated banking or insurance activity. Pay the reservation fee and obtain a written name reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in English (and optional Samoan translation)
Signed confirmation of no prohibited or misleading name elements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for resemblance or prohibited word, file a written objection with the Registrar within 7 days, submit a revised name list, or request a formal administrative review of the refusal decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of registered agent and registered office confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent in Samoa (approved by SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute an engagement agreement with a SIFA-licensed registered agent. The agent must provide a physical registered office address in Samoa, consent to act, and maintain the statutory registers at that address. Collect the agent's consent letter and the address particulars needed for Form IC-1.
required_dossiers: Registered agent's formal consent to act
Copy of the registered agent's SIFA license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent withdraws consent, appoint a substitute licensed agent and file a Notice of Change of Registered Agent and Registered Office within 14 days to avoid administrative strike-off.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of charter documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in Samoa or recognized foreign notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with the International Companies Act 1987. Have the incorporator(s) sign before a notary public. If signed outside Samoa, the signature must be duly notarized and apostilled or legalized for Samoa. Two original counterparts must be prepared for SIFA and the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Form IC-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is rejected by SIFA due to defective attestation, re-execute the document with an adhesive stamp or a supplementary certification and file a corrective declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation application and statutory declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Form IC-1, the statutory declaration of compliance signed by the registered agent, and the prescribed fee to the Registrar. The application can be submitted electronically through the SIFA portal or as a physical dossier. The Registrar will examine the charter for compliance with the Act and, if satisfactory, issue a Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Payment confirmation of the incorporation fee
Consent of each director and officer (if not included in Form IC-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query, respond in writing within 14 calendar days with a corrected executed document or a waiver request. If the application is rejected, appeal to the Minister of Finance within the time limit stated in the requisition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation organization meeting and board appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or pass written resolutions) to adopt the minutes, issue shares, appoint directors and officers, approve the opening of bank accounts, and adopt the clinical trial service agreement template. The board must also approve the appointment of the registered agent and the availability of the physical registered office.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes or resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent or bank requires a certified copy of the first board resolution, have the company secretary certify the resolution and affix the company seal; if the meeting is challenged, file a written waiver signed by all directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for annual government fees and corporate records maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA and Samoa Ministry of Revenue (for occurrence-based tax filing obligations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual return with SIFA and pay the annual international company fee before the anniversary of incorporation. Maintain the registered office, share register, director register, and minutes at the registered agent's office. Retain originals of all clinical trial agreements, financial records, and board minutes for at least 7 years.
required_dossiers: Up-to-date registers of directors, members, and charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is filed late, remit the late penalty within 30 days and file a letter of explanation to avoid automatic strike-off; apply for reinstatement within 12 months if the company is struck off.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health Samoa – Health Research and Ethics Committee (HREC) and Clinical Trial Regulatory Unit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Clinical Trial Sponsorship and CRO Operating Permit (under the Health Ordinance 1959 and National Health Research Policy)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa – Planning and Urban Management Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (Registration) for office-only CRO services; Category A (Full EIA Report) required if the CRO operates a clinical laboratory, specimen storage, or any physical biological facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero discharge of untreated biomedical waste; compliance with the Waste Management Act 2010 and the Samoa National Environmental Standards; wastewater pH maintained between 6.0 and 9.0; no discharge of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) above 50 ppm in indoor occupational air; biomedical waste autoclaved at 121°C/15 psi for 30 minutes before removal by an approved waste contractor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority; structural load clearance from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure; occupational health clearance from the Occupational Safety and Health Division of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour for office-based CRO activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue of the Independent State of Samoa (MOR); official e-services portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Samoa International Company ('IC') is not required to obtain a Taxpayer Identification Number for its statutorily exempt offshore business. If the foreign-owned IC nevertheless becomes subject to a Samoa VAGST registration or withholding obligation, it must lodge a written registration application with the Ministry of Revenue, attaching: (i) a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation; (ii) the IC Constitution or Memorandum of Association; (iii) written confirmation of the registered agent in Samoa; (iv) beneficial ownership details and passport copies of directors/shareholders; and (v) a statement of the taxable activities intended to be carried on in Samoa. MOR will issue a Samoa Taxpayer Identification Number and, where appropriate, a VAGST registration number upon complete lodgement. No TIN is required solely for the offshore CRO management business of an exempt International Company.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity election. The Samoa International Company is automatically classified as a tax-exempt offshore entity under the International Companies Act 1987. There is no domestic income-tax equivalent to a CFC election, branch tax election, or partnership pass-through election for the IC; this exemption is mandatory and cannot be waived. VAGST election is limited to compulsory or voluntary registration where a taxable supply in Samoa is being made.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST – Value Added Goods and Services Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 annual taxable turnover; a non-resident supplier carrying on a taxable activity in Samoa is registrable when this threshold is met or exceeded. A Samoa International Company supplying only offshore CRO and clinical-trial management services does not create a Samoa VAGST registration nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently require real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, electronic invoice stamping, or mandatory API connectivity. A VAGST-registered supplier must issue a tax invoice containing the seller's name, tax identification number, invoice serial number and date, description of supply, taxable amount, rate, and VAGST charged. The Ministry of Revenue accepts standard PDF/physical invoices and does not mandate an approved digital clearance system for export zero-rated claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A VAGST-registered CRO may zero-rate the supply of clinical trial management, biostatistics, data management, regulatory affairs, and related consultancy services when those services are supplied to a non-resident sponsor for use and enjoyment entirely outside Samoa. Tangible exportations from Samoa — including clinical trial kits, biological samples, and investigational medical devices shipped to a foreign laboratory — also qualify for zero-rating where the exporter maintains documentary proof of physical exportation within the prescribed period. The claim is allowed only if the supply is not made in connection with a taxable activity carried on in Samoa by the recipient and the documentation is held before the relevant taxable period return is filed.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry of Revenue may audit zero-rated export transactions and require the taxpayer to produce the full customs, shipping, bank remittance, and contractual evidence trail. A fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claim will be reversed by assessment of a VAGST shortfall, with penalties of up to 100% of the tax evaded, interest for late payment, and recovery of any refund as a debt due to the State. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion under the Tax Administration Act 2012 may be brought against the IC, its directors, and its tax agent. Claimants should retain all export and remittance records for a minimum of seven years to substantiate every 180-day outward payment cycle.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), also styled Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa, operating under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984 and administering the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Exchange Control Regulations 1978, and the Financial Institutions Act 1996 (as amended); CBS licenses all authorized dealer banks and supervises Samoa's foreign exchange, AML/CFT, and payments infrastructure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a managed currency that is not fully convertible. Current-account transactions, including cross-border CRO service fees, pass-through clinical-site reimbursements, and disbursements under a documented clinical trial master service agreement, may be settled through an authorized dealer bank without case-by-case CBS approval provided the dealer receives supporting contracts, invoices, and the standard exchange-control declaration. Capital-account transactions, including equity injections into the Samoa International Company, loan top-ups, and inbound acquisition funding, require prior CBS approval via the authorized dealer. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are lawful but subject to documentary hurdles: audited Samoan financial statements evidencing distributable profits, a tax clearance from the Samoan tax authority (Ministry for Revenue), withholding tax compliance on dividend distributions where the IC's exempt status does not apply, confirmation from the Registrar of International and Foreign Companies that the entity has no outstanding annual fees, and CBS exchange-control application processing. Because the IC enjoys an exempt tax status, the practical convertibility obstacle is documentary rather than fiscal, but any inbound USD that is not accompanied by a dealer-filed purpose narrative will be quarantined in a suspense capital account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All proceeds from exports of goods and services, expressly including Clinical Trial CRO milestone fees invoiced in USD, must be repatriated to Samoa within 90 days of the due date and 100% of the foreign currency receipts must be offered for surrender and conversion into WST through an authorized dealer bank. CBS retention approval may be obtained where demonstrable contractual need exists to retain USD operating balances, such as committed payments to offshore central laboratories; without retention approval, the CRO treasury must negotiate each inbound wire into WST at the dealer's telegraphic-transfer buying rate and maintain a contemporaneous surrender schedule reconciled with each MT103 credit. Failure to surrender is an exchange-control offence under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and can trigger penalties, forced conversion, and suspension of the dealer relationship; the CRO should therefore never allow sponsor funds to accumulate in an unapproved offshore EMI account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account (WST/USD) with segregated Capital Escrow sub-ledger

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Limited — Samoa Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational WST Account with USD facility via BSP Group correspondent network
Operational WST-only Account with limited USD clearing capacity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for primary custody treasury; MEDIUM for auxiliary disbursement only. Samoa has no statutory EMI or fintech licensing category; any deposit-taking or money-transfer business requires a CBS banking or financial-institution license under the Financial Institutions Act 1996. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise Business, Payoneer, or Airwallex may be used to receive sponsor payments and disburse international site payments, but they cannot operate as the CRO's authorized dealer, do not satisfy CBS surrender and reporting obligations, and create reportable fund movements outside authorized channels; the International Company should maintain its principal treasury at ANZ or BSP and use EMIs, if at all, only as a named-invoice collection conduit with automatic sweep to the Samoan dealer account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is mandated for directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories of the Samoa International Company. Both ANZ Samoa and BSP Samoa require an in-branch face-to-face KYC interview in Samoa for IC structures; a fully remote or video-only onboarding path is not available. For foreign directors who cannot travel, the banks accept notarized identification, apostilled constitutional and status documents issued by the Registrar of International and Foreign Companies, and a formal legal-entity KYC pack vetted by a Samoa-licensed lawyer; however, at least one physical interview must be attended in Samoa by the resident director, registered agent, or the entity's designated AML-certified introducer. Practical planning: schedule at least two physical treasury-relationship trips and maintain a Samoa-resident director or registered agent to keep the account in good standing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (nominee shareholders, multi-tier offshore trusts, historic bearer-share structures).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Register of Members and Beneficial Ownership Register filed with the Registrar; natural-person BO declaration identifying every holder of 10% or more; redacted trust deed and trustee resolution for trust-held shares; legal opinion from Samoan counsel confirming no bearer shares and no unresolved nominee ambiguity; apostilled Constitution and Certificate of Good Standing; source-of-wealth narrative per BO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value, high-frequency international wires inconsistent with the ISIC 7490 clinical CRO description.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Master Clinical Trial Services Agreement with the named sponsor; milestone and pass-through payment schedule; project contracts with clinical sites, institutional review boards, central laboratories, and principal investigators; CBS purpose-code narratives for each inbound and outbound payment; sponsor's bank reference and sanctions-clearance evidence; annual CRO activity report demonstrating protocol management, site monitoring, data management, and biostatistics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial capital injection and operating float.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of source-account bank statements; board resolution authorizing share issuance and allotment; subscription agreement; statutory declaration of source of wealth; professional bank reference for the funding entity; if funded by a related trust or holding company, the trust deed and consolidation of underlying commercial activity evidencing legitimate wealth generation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived 'shell' status of the Samoa International Company and absence of economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Status Certificate and Certificate of Registration issued by the Registrar of International and Foreign Companies; economic-substance narrative describing real people, real functions (protocol design, safety monitoring, site liaison, biostatistics), and real Samoan anchors (registered office, resident agent, local director where applicable, Samoan bank signatories); IC tax-exempt status acknowledgment from the Ministry for Revenue; confirmation that audited accounts are prepared when required and annual regulatory fees are current.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: sponsor or parent R&D treasury sends USD via SWIFT MT103 to the Samoa IC's account at ANZ or BSP, quoting the beneficiary name exactly as registered, the IC's account number and BIC, and payment narrative 'IC share capital subscription — WS_IC — Exchange Control Application ref [dealer/CBS reference]'; the authorized dealer files the CBS inward-capital application before or immediately upon receipt; capital funds are posted to a segregated Capital Escrow sub-ledger and transferred to Operations only upon board resolution and CBS confirmation; the dealer issues a Negotiation/Conversion Advice applying the telegraphic-transfer buying rate if conversion to WST is required, and any excess over the approved amount is cleared under a current-account service-fee invoice rather than retained offshore. Verification pack: executed subscription and allotment resolution, board minutes, source-account statements, sponsor's sanctions-clearance certificate, and the CBS stamped application. If the capital is retained in USD, a CBS retention approval is required and the balance must be reconciled monthly to the dealer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for CRO trial disbursements: (i) SWIFT MT103 for each site, laboratory, institutional review board, and investigator payment, with purpose code 'business/professional services 7490' and full invoice and serial references; (ii) MT202 COV for large interbank cover legs where the USD clearing bank differs from the beneficiary's bank (Samoa has no local USD clearing, so USD moves clear via ANZ Sydney/Auckland or BSP Australia/PNG correspondents); (iii) domestic WST payments to Samoa-resident investigators and sites via the CBS-overseen interbank settlement system or ANZ/BSP internal transfer; (iv) Commercial Letters of Credit are not standard for CRO services but may be used where a sponsor jurisdiction mandates collateralization, with presentation documents comprising the commercial invoice, signed milestone acceptance certificate, CRO status certificate, and insurance certificate, opened through the dealer bank with CBS exchange-control endorsement for services. All outbound instructions must carry accurate purpose codes and be mirrored in the dealer's monthly exchange-control return to CBS; pass-through funds for clinical sites should be segregated from the IC's own fee margin to preserve the Low_Risk_Standard AML classification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CBS-authorized spot and forward foreign-exchange contracts with an authorized dealer bank, with tenor generally up to 12 months, covering documented CRO contract receivables and payables and supported by the milestone schedule as underlying exposure evidence.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing WST/USD, permissible only with prior CBS exchange-control approval and only for genuine hedging of a contracted clinical-trial foreign-currency exposure; speculative NDF positions are prohibited for a Samoa International Company.

Cross-currency swaps, permissible on an ad hoc basis only after CBS authorization and in practice unavailable onshore; the treasury should instead mirror-match USD/WST assets and liabilities and align invoicing currency with sponsor funding currency to eliminate swap dependency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Renewal Fee (Annual Licence Fee) for International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (filed through licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the incorporation anniversary; payable on or before the anniversary date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% per annum late-payment penalty on arrears; after 90 days the Registrar may serve a strike-off notice; non-payment triggers administrative dissolution and restoration requires arrears, penalties, and reinstatement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Compliance Declaration and Statutory File Attestation by the Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies via licensed international trust and company service provider; held in agent's statutory file and produced on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Co-filed with the annual renewal fee before each incorporation anniversary; updated within 14 days of any director, member, or UBO change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalties under the International Companies Act 1987 for defective statutory records; repeated default supports strike-off; agent licence suspension for wilful non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Annual Refresh (UBO confirmation for clinical-trial CRO holding entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent / AML compliance officer (financial intelligence record; no public registry filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At annual renewal review and within 14 days of any share transfer, change in control, or alteration of beneficial interest
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Enforcement under the AML/CFT Act 2018; fines on agent and company; suspension of distribution or share-transfer processing until register is remedied.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a standard exempted International Company; audit is voluntary under the International Companies Act 1987 unless the entity holds a regulated financial licence, its articles mandate audit, or the Registrar orders an inspection.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Record-keeping under the International Companies Act 1987; voluntary audits follow IFRS; no prescribed Samoa Local GAAP for International Companies; no domestic tax filings required while the tax-exempt status is maintained.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Registered agent holds a beneficial ownership register and performs an annual KYC refresh at each renewal; share transfers are valid only on registration in the register of members; the agent must be notified within 14 days of any significant ownership or control change; no public UBO disclosure applies to International Companies.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Beneficial Ownership Register (maintained by registered agent)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – 900 per annum typical market range for licensed Samoa registered agent and registered office services; USD 1,000 – 1,500 for enhanced AML/UBO dossier handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 6,000 for a voluntary IFRS audit of a low-volume CRO holding company; zero if the audit exemption is exercised.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% statutory exemption for International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987; standard domestic resident corporate rate 25%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full income tax, capital gains tax, and withholding tax exemption for International Companies; only fixed annual government fee payable to Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); exemption conditional on no Samoan-resident business and no Samoan-source income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return (Form IC-AR) under the International Companies Act 1987; filed with the Registrar of International Companies through SIFA; electronic filing portal or hard-copy submission via licensed registered agent
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 calendar days after the anniversary of incorporation; annual government fee payable on the same due date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International Company registration number and name
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert exact name as per Certificate of Incorporation; no deviation permitted
Must be a physical service address maintained by the licensed registered agent in Samoa
Appointed Samoan-licensed agent; non-resident cannot self-appoint
Disclose full names, nationalities, and residential addresses; nominee directors must be identified as such
Provide beneficial owner details per AML requirements; bearer shares prohibited
State 'contract research organization and clinical trial management services for non-resident biopharmaceutical clients'; confirm no Samoan-source income
Confirm no business with Samoan residents, no local real estate, no banking business, and no domestic tax liability
Confirm whether the company carries on relevant activities, IP holding, or intra-group service functions subject to ESR requirements

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty per International Companies Fees Regulations (approximately SAT 500); continued default for 3 months triggers automatic striking-off from the Register; restoration requires payment of all arrears, sat penalty, and reinstatement fee; late annual fee accrues monthly surcharge until settled

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for International Companies (statutory exemption); standard Samoa corporate withholding tax rate on dividends is 15% for both residents and non-residents
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement, the IC must (1) submit a written claim to SIFA with a completed Form DTA-1, (2) provide Certificate of Incorporation, register extract, and beneficial ownership declaration, (3) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Ministry of Revenue through SIFA, (4) transmit the authenticated TRC and treaty claim to the payer or overseas tax authority, and (5) update the claim annually; relief is denied if substance or beneficial ownership conditions are not met
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: IC statutory exemption: 0% on both royalty and interest outbound payments from Samoa; domestic statutory rate is 15% for both categories; treaty rates typically 5% to 10% subject to DTA provisions and beneficial ownership confirmation

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory Local File or Master File threshold applies to International Companies because they are tax-exempt; however, SIFA economic substance guidance and prudential practice require an arm's-length transfer pricing documentation package for cross-border related-party service transactions above SAT 10 million (approximately EUR 500,000), including CRO service agreements, fee benchmarks, cost allocation models, and functional risk profiles
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) Act 2018 applies to SIFA-licensed International Companies. Contract research organization and clinical trial management activities that derive income from intra-group services, service centre functions, or intellectual property holding are classified as relevant activities. The IC must satisfy: (a) direction and management exercised in Samoa, (b) adequate number of qualified employees, (c) adequate operating expenditure in Samoa, (d) physical presence through the registered agent, and (e) filing of an annual ESR return with SIFA. Failure to meet the economic substance test and annual ESR compliance (Form ESR-1) constitutes a serious offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Abuse of IC Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting clinical trial services or other commercial activity with Samoan residents, deriving Samoan-source income, or using the International Company as a sham conduit for domestic operations while claiming the 0% exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Forfeiture of tax-exempt status; assessment of all back taxes at the 25% corporate rate plus capital gains and withholding taxes; interest at 10% per annum and a penalty of 100% to 150% of the tax evaded under the Income Tax Act 2012; monetary fines up to SAT 1,000,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax where the evasion was deliberate or reckless; civil restitution of diverted funds; disqualification from acting as a director for up to 10 years; travel bans and imprisonment up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the IC with no real economic presence, minimal personnel, no Samoa-based management activity, total delegation to nominee directors, or failing to file the ESR-1 annual substance declaration while asserting CRO or IP-related activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty under the ESR Act 2018 of up to SAT 500,000 for an initial breach and up to SAT 1,000,000 with imprisonment of directors for repeated breach; SIFA may strike off the company, revoke the international company licence, and assess deemed income at the full corporate rate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for all penalties and outstanding government fees; cease-and-desist orders; travel restrictions; obstruction of company divestiture; custodial sentence up to 10 years if false declarations are certified

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the CRO business cash flows to launder drug trial proceeds, processing payments for sanctioned sponsors, maintaining undisclosed beneficial owners, or failing to conduct client due diligence under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to SAT 5,000,000 for the corporate entity; confiscation of funds under proceeds of crime provisions; suspension or revocation of the SIFA licence and banking relationship; freezing of the IC's assets; statutory penalty per transaction for unreported suspicious activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and the registered agent face criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 14 years; personal confiscation orders; travel bans and 10-year prohibition on holding financial services positions; civil fiduciary claims for loss suffered by third-party investors

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Transfer Pricing and Sham Arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fabricating mark-ups, circular invoice flows with associated clinical sites, artificially diverting trial revenue into the tax-exempt IC while paying inflated management fees, or mispricing intercompany CRO services to shift profits from a taxable jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization and taxing of diverted profits at 25%; transfer pricing adjustments with interest; penalty of 50% of the under-reported gross revenue; reciprocal disclosures under the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance and exchange of information with treaty partners
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who orchestrated the sham are personally liable for the recharacterized tax and penalties; criminal sanctions for aiding tax evasion; civil clawback actions in the jurisdiction of the parent sponsor; travel bans and extradition risk under mutual legal assistance treaties; imprisonment up to 7 years
